explanation: God's reaction to human disobedience and sin, often involving suffering and difficulties.
An Old Testament people with whom God made a covenant; in the book of Amos, it refers to the northern tribes of the kingdom of Israel.
A title used for God, emphasizing his sovereignty and authority over all.
A change of heart and mind where a person turns away from sin and toward God.
The principle of acting rightly and uprightly, both in relation to God and other people.
God's fair evaluation and handling of human behavior, especially in relation to sin and disobedience.
Lack of food as a result of God's punishment and warning to the people to turn from their sins.
Lack of rain and water, leading to poor harvests and suffering; also part of God's punishment and warnings.
A contagious and deadly disease that affects humans and animals, which in the book of Amos is part of God's punishment.
